How does one get into sales with no experience?

My company used to hire salesman to sell my products, these were people that had years of sales experience, yet they couldn't sell their way out of a paper bag. I ended up doing all the selling and they would get the commission. So, after a while, I dispensed with these "salesmen".

Their biggest obstacle to making the sale was that they - wanted to be liked all the time, they didn't dare offend a prospect/client in any way. This means they could not challenge the prospect/client to overcome natural sales resistance. Sometimes all it takes to make the sale is to push a pen across the table and say something like - Don't you think we've we've talked about this long enough? All we need to get started helping your company is your signature on that contract.

Look up the ABCs of selling.

I used to work in the upstream oil industry building and servicing electromechanical equipment. That's how I got started. I had a pretty nice career going netting just under 6 figures before the great collapse of 2015. Now I build, install, service, and maintain automated building systems, low voltage electric systems, data/voice/telecom networks, security, surveillance, access control, and audio-visual systems. I do everything from structured cabling to assembling and repairing circuit boards to working on electric motors and a host of other electronic equipment. I also have a private security license and went to college for electronics and multimedia production, but I couldn't pass math so I flunked out, lol.

Tons of sales jobs at all levels. Forget about being an expert in the product. True sales guys can jump from industry to industry. Learn everything you can about how to make friends and influence people (and yeah, read the book) and learn about closing. Learn about how to deal with questions like "let me think about it" and shit like that.

Focus 80% on relationships and closing and 20% on the product. You can always say "I'll find out and get back to you on that" if they ask something you don't know.

As for where to start... literally any level. Don't do it for the job or money, but the experience of being chad sales. Once you get enough confidence that you aren't posting questions like this to goats, you'll be able to sell yourself to your next employer for more pay.

It's like politics. You have to convince people they want what you have. Fear is the biggest motivator. As an electrician, selling is super easy if you have no scruples. "There is a possibility that your house could burn down" is a line I've heard too many times. I personally will only use it if there is actually a danger of it that needs to be remedied. I'm the type that can listen to a need and tailor a solution for it. I can't sell a person on what they don't want. I never learned how to do that and don't want to.
